g.data-info: A thimble of loose cells covering the tip that protects the meristem as the root pushes through soil; outer cells are worn off.
Meristematic region of small, thin-walled cells with dense cytoplasm and large nuclei that divide repeatedly.
A small group of slowly dividing cells at the tip of the meristem that can replace damaged initials.
Cells here stop dividing and grow longer by taking up water, pushing the root tip forward.
Cells differentiate into permanent tissues such as epidermis, cortex and vascular tissue.
Central strand where xylem and phloem differentiate behind the growing tip.
Outgrowths of epidermal cells in the maturation zone that absorb water and minerals; older hairs are longer.
